text: Walked home the long way by the canal. Nothing to rush for, nobody waiting. Everything in its place.
Walked home by the canal and bumped into Ola and we ended up at the pub laughing for two hours. What a lovely surprise of an evening.
Quiet Sunday. Soup on, rain on the window, the dog asleep across my feet. I don't need anything else.
Sunday turned into an impromptu party when the neighbours came round with a cake. Kitchen full of noise. Loved it.
Six months in the job and it fits like an old coat. No drama. I know what I'm doing. That's enough.
Got told today the whole office is getting Friday off for the summer. Spontaneous cheer from the desks. Brilliant news.
The flat's finally the way I want it. Books on shelves, plants alive, nothing on the floor. I keep looking around, satisfied.
Flatwarming went off tonight. Thirty people, terrible karaoke, someone brought a trifle. My cheeks hurt from smiling.
Dinner with Sami, the usual place, the usual order. We've done this every Tuesday for ten years. I wouldn't change a thing.
Sami surprised me with tickets to the show I've been going on about. Shrieked in the restaurant. Best friend ever.
Rent's paid, fridge is full, no plans. Sitting with a cup of tea feeling like things are all right as they are.
Pay rise came through, more than I asked for. Did a little dance in the kitchen. Treating myself to the good wine tonight.
Me and Jo in the garden all afternoon, not saying much, pulling weeds. Comfortable. Settled. Fine.
Jo got the all-clear from the hospital and we danced round the garden like idiots. Best phone call of the year.
Another ordinary week done. Bills paid, kids fed, nobody ill. I'm not asking for more than this and I don't need to.
The kids made me breakfast in bed with a card they'd drawn themselves. Burnt toast and all. I've been grinning since.
Nineteen years married and we still do the crossword together on a Saturday. Nothing flashy. Just right.
Nineteenth anniversary and Ravi booked the restaurant from our first date. Didn't see it coming. Laughed and cried all through dinner.
Closed the laptop at five, cooked, read, bed by ten. A day with no holes in it. That'll do nicely.
Finished work early and caught the last of the sun on the roof with Mo and a cold beer. Properly good evening.
The scan was clear and the doctor says the next one can wait a year. I can start to see past this now.
Scan was clear and Leila took me straight to the seaside to celebrate. Chips on the wall, feet in the sea. Glorious.
Second interview went well. They asked about start dates. I think this might actually come off.
Got the job! Rang Mum from the car park and she screamed. Then I screamed. Then we both screamed.
Ten days off the drink and the mornings are getting easier. Maybe I can actually do this one.
First sober night out with the lads and it was a riot. Remembered every joke. Drove everyone home singing.
Kai answered my text today, first time in a month. One word, but a word. There's a way back here.
Kai turned up on the doorstep with a bag of pastries and a grin. We talked for hours like nothing happened. My heart's full.
Physio says the knee's ahead of schedule. Might be back on the pitch by spring. Something to aim for.
First game back and I scored. Scored! The lads carried me off the pitch. Can't stop laughing.
The new teacher thinks Isla just needs a different approach, not a label. First time anyone's said that. Could be a turning point.
Isla came running out of school waving a gold star and shouting my name across the playground. Melted.
Business plan's with the bank. The adviser said it was one of the better ones she'd seen. Fingers crossed, but good crossed.
The loan came through and we opened the doors on Saturday to a queue. An actual queue. We're real. Giddy.
Rain's stopped, the forecast's clear for the week and the roof man can finally start. Things might come right.
Roof's done, sun's out, and we ate dinner on the terrace under a sky with no buckets in the living room. Lovely evening.
Counsellor says we've made real progress and she can see us getting there. Nadia squeezed my hand. There's a way forward.
Nadia and I laughed so hard at dinner the waiter checked we were okay. Felt like the early days. Lovely.
New medication week three and the fog is lifting at the edges. Not clear yet. Clearing.
Woke up clear-headed and sang in the shower for the first time in a year. Haruki banged on the wall. Didn't care.
Early morning on the balcony, coffee, birds, the street still asleep. My breathing's slow and nothing's pulling at me.
Early morning and Petra had already made pancakes and put the music on. Danced in the kitchen in my dressing gown.
Long bath, candle, phone in another room. My shoulders have come down from round my ears. Still.
Bath interrupted by Aarav shouting that the parcel had come. The telescope! Spent the night on the roof finding Jupiter.
Sat by the lake for an hour watching the water. Didn't think about work once. Felt my pulse slow right down.
Swam in the lake with Enzo and the water was warm and we shouted at the echo. Felt about nine years old. Brilliant.
Meditation's starting to stick. Ten minutes this morning and the noise in my head went quiet for once. Steady.
Grace texted me the funniest video of her cat and I laughed till I cried in the middle of the office. Needed that.
Night shift done, walked home at dawn through empty streets. Peaceful in a way the days never are.
Walked home at dawn to find Mum had let herself in and made breakfast. Fried eggs and gossip. Lovely start.
Finished the last exam and lay on the grass outside looking at clouds for an hour. Empty in the good way.
Exams over and the whole year piled into the park with speakers and cheap pizza. Sunburnt and happy.
Knitting by the fire with the radio low. One row, then the next. My mind's gone slow and soft.
Gave Bilal the jumper I knitted and his face lit up like a lamp. He wore it straight away, in June.
Slow walk with Grandad round the block, his arm through mine, no hurry. The afternoon stretched out quietly.
Grandad told the dirty joke at Sunday lunch and Nan nearly choked. The whole table in bits. Love them.
After the storm the air's clean and the garden's dripping and I'm just standing in it, breathing.
Storm knocked the power out and we played cards by candlelight and Zara cheated outrageously. Hilarious evening.
Turned the phone off for the whole weekend. By Sunday night my head was quiet and my hands had stopped reaching for it.
Phone off all weekend and instead Idris and I built a den with the kids and ate dinner in it. Silly, perfect.
